title: GPFedRec: Graph-Guided Personalization for Federated Recommendation

problem.claim: Federated recommendation seeks to provide recommendation services while preserving privacy, and user-relation graphs could enhance federated recommendations.

gap.claim: Constructing a user-relation graph while preserving data-locality-based privacy in federated settings remains an open challenge.

contributions.claim: GPFedRec constructs a user-relation graph at the server from user-specific personalized item embeddings without accessing users' interaction records.
The method locally fine-tunes personalized item embeddings on each device and constructs the graph by measuring similarity among client-specific item embeddings.
GPFedRec uses graph-guided aggregation together with the federated optimization framework.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe GPFedRec as a novel graph-guided personalization method for federated recommendation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets demonstrate superior performance for GPFedRec.
The authors report that GPFedRec generally improves existing federated recommendation methods as a plugin while keeping user privacy safe.
The authors report that code is available in a GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated recommendation provides privacy-preserving recommendation services, and user-relation graphs are a promising enhancement.
Constructing user-relation graphs while preserving data-locality-based privacy is challenging.
GPFedRec constructs a server-side user-relation graph from locally fine-tuned client-specific item embeddings without accessing interaction records.
Graph-guided aggregation combines the user-relation graph with federated optimization.
The authors report superior performance on five benchmark datasets and general improvement of existing federated recommendation methods as a privacy-preserving plugin.

source_observation.claim: Client-specific personalized item embeddings are used to measure user similarity and construct a relation graph without accessing interaction records.

interpretation.claim: Privacy-preserving federated personalization can use derived representations as coordination signals while keeping raw interaction data local.

application.claim: In federated systems, consider server-side relationship modeling from locally generated representations when raw-data sharing is restricted.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish privacy guarantees beyond the stated absence of interaction-record access.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five benchmark datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the graph construction algorithm, aggregation details, or privacy threat model.
